table_recommendations.recommendation: Drug-eluting stents are recommended in preference to bare metal stents in all cases.

In patients with spontaneous coronary artery dissection, PCI is recommended only for patients with symptoms and signs of ongoing myocardial ischaemia, a large area of myocardium in jeopardy, and reduced antegrade flow.
Intravascular imaging should be considered to guide PCI.
Coronary artery bypass grafting should be considered in patients with an occluded IRA when PPCI is not feasible/unsuccessful and there is a large area of myocardium in jeopardy.
Intravascular imaging (preferably optical coherence tomography) may be considered in patients with ambiguous culprit lesions.
The routine use of thrombus aspiration is not recommended.

content.abbreviations_and_notes: IRA = infarct-related artery; PCI = percutaneous coronary intervention; PPCI = primary percutaneous coronary intervention. aClass of recommendation. bLevel of evidence. © ESC 2023

recommendations_box.recommendation: Radial access is recommended as the standard approach, unless there are overriding procedural considerations.
PCI with stent deployment in the IRA during the index procedure is recommended in patients undergoing PPCI.
